item.title: Geometry of a class of $\varphi$-minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^2\times \mathbb{R}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.27187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a class of $\varphi$-minimal surfaces in the product space $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{R}$, that is, weighted minimal surfaces whose corresponding weight is determined by a smooth potential function $\varphi$ that depends only on the height coordinate relative to the factor $\mathbb{R}$. Under monotonicity, concavity, and asymptotic conditions on $\varphi$, we obtain a complete classification of connected, properly embedded $\varphi$-minimal surfaces that are invariant under isometries of $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{R}$ acting trivially on $\mathbb{R}$ and by rotations or parabolic translations on $\mathbb{H}^2$. Finally, we establish several non-existence results for $\varphi$-minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^2 \times \mathbb{R}$, either by using properties of the height function or by applying the tangency principle together with suitable invariant surfaces as barriers.
item.dc:creator: Katianny Rosa Freitas, Jo\~ao Paulo dos Santos, Ant\'onio Mart\'inez

item.title: $L^{p}$-parabolicity of Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.27302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the $L^p$-parabolicity of a Riemannian manifold in terms of a unified theory of nonlinear $L^p$-capacities, for the whole range $1\leq p\leq \infty$. For example, the \(L^{1}\)-parabolicity is equivalent to the usual notion of parabolicity/recurrence, while \(L^{2}\)-parabolicity is equivalent to biparabolicity. For any $1\leq p\leq \infty,$ the $L^p$-parabolicity turns out to be equivalent to the $L^q$-Liouville property for positive superharmonic functions, where $p$ and $q$ are H\"older conjugate exponents. We also provide a new capacitary characterization of the $L^1$-Liouville property. Finally we obtain an almost optimal volume growth condition for the $L^p$-parabolicity for $1<p\leq 2$ as well as a sharp volume condition for all $1<p<\infty$ for manifolds of non-negative Ricci curvature and for model manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Grigor'yan, Leandro F. Pessoa, Alberto G. Setti

item.title: Triviality of $K$-homology classes of Euler characteristic operators of stratified pseudomanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.27476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the $K$-homology classes of the Euler characteristic operators associated with the minimal and maximal ideal boundary conditions of the de Rham differential on the regular part of a connected compact Thom-Mather stratified pseudomanifold, equipped with an adapted metric, are trivial beyond their indices. These indices are the Euler characteristics of the corresponding $L^2$-cohomologies. This generalizes a result of J. Rosenberg for manifolds. The proof uses Witten deformation of the de Rham operator associated with a stratified Morse function, following the work of \'Alvarez L\'opez and Calaza.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadali Aligholi

item.title: Rotations, Shears, and Two-Generation on Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.27507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every round sphere $S^n$, $n\ge2$, we exhibit two explicit divergence-free vector fields whose flows generate a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $\SDiff_0(S^n)$. One generator is an elementary planar rotation, \[ A=R_{12}, \] while the other combines a linearly modulated planar rotation with a chain of adjacent planar rotations: \[ B=x_3R_{12}+\sum_{k=2}^n R_{k,k+1}. \] Thus two one-parameter groups suffice, and two is the smallest possible number. The proof separates naturally into two steps. We first show that the $n$ adjacent rotations \[ R_{12},R_{23},\ldots,R_{n,n+1} \] together with the shear $x_3R_{12}$ generate, through their flows, a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $\SDiff_0(S^n)$. The infinitesimal argument is organized by transverse vector spherical harmonics. For $n\ge4$ the relevant harmonic spaces are irreducible $SO(n+1)$-modules; on $S^2$ the argument reduces to the Hamiltonian/Poisson formalism; and on $S^3$ the transverse harmonic spaces split into two curl eigenspaces. We then show that all $n+1$ of these vector fields lie in the Lie algebra generated by $A$ and $B$. A Casimir operator separates the quadratic shear from the linear rotational terms, after which the remaining rotations can be recovered successively. Finally, standard approximation formulas for flows convert the Lie-algebraic generation result into $C^\infty$ density in $\SDiff_0(S^n)$.
item.dc:creator: Dennis DeTurck

item.title: Gauge theory on Cohomogeneity One Spin(7)-Manifolds from Aloff--Wallach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.27686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We begin a systematic study of $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-instantons on complete non-compact cohomogeneity one $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-manifolds with Aloff--Wallach spaces $N_{k,l}=\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{U}(1)_{k,l}$ as principal orbits. We provide a complete classification of admissible principal $\mathrm{U}(1)$- and $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-bundles and smooth bounded solutions to the $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-instanton equation on them. We study bubbling phenomena for the constructed $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-instantons and discuss the compactification of the moduli space of $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-instantons in both the ALC and AC settings.
item.dc:creator: Hanci Chi, Enric Sol\'e-Farr\'e

item.title: Eliminating the Higgs field and perturbing Yang-Mills connections in cone Yang-Mills theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.27734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the configurations of the cone Yang-Mills functional over a closed connected manifold. We show that the Euler-Lagrange equation from variations in the Higgs field is always uniquely solvable for $\zeta \neq 0$, allowing us to eliminate one of the two equations from the theory. By eliminating the equation, we obtain a family of ``effective cone Yang-Mills functionals'' on the space of connection 1-forms indexed by $\zeta$, which reduce to Yang-Mills theory when $\zeta = 0$. This suggests a way to nontrivially deform the Yang-Mills moduli space. We take the first step towards this deformation by showing that, near certain critical points of the Yang-Mills functional, there is a family of smooth connections $A_t$ which satisfy the $t\zeta$-cone Yang-Mills equations.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Delgado

item.title: Non-null ruled surfaces and pseudo hyper-dual tangent sphere bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.27809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, the tangent bundles of hyper-dual pseudo spheres are defined. Then, a new family of non-null ruled surfaces associated with hyper-dual Lorentzian curves is defined via the E.Study hyper-map in Minkowski space and the definitions of the tangent bundles of hyper-dual pseudo spheres. Within this framework, the resulting non-null ruled surfaces are classified. Necessary and sufficient conditions for developability are obtained with their geometric interpretations in terms of hyper-dual Lorentzian curves and arc-length parameters. Moreover, explicit examples are presented to verify the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Emel Karaca, Senem \"Ozt\"urk

item.title: An $L^1$ bound for Ricci curvature on K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.28142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a uniform $L^1$ bound for Ricci curvature on noncollapsed K\"ahler manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below. The proof combines the codimension two neck decomposition and entropy estimates with local K\"ahler geometry on regular balls. The key step is a linear control of the Ricci integral on a regular ball by the entropy pinching, obtained from a decomposition of the scalar-curvature integral that exploits the K\"ahler structure.
item.dc:creator: Wenshuai Jiang, Gang Liu

item.title: On the spectrum of the biharmonic Steklov operator with Neumann boundary conditions acting on forms of the unit Euclidean ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.28181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the spectrum of the biharmonic Steklov operator with Neumann boundary conditions acting on differential $p$-forms over the unit Euclidean ball. We apply it to test how far one of Kuttler-Sigillito inequalities is from being optimal.
item.dc:creator: Rodolphe Abou Assali

item.title: K\"ahler-Ricci Shrinkers with Nonnegative Ricci Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.28238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every complete K\"ahler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature is holomorphically isometric to $\mathbb{C}^k\times N^{n-k}$ for some $0\le k\le n$, where $\mathbb{C}^k$ is the Gaussian shrinker and $N$ is a compact K\"ahler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature. As a corollary, every complete K\"ahler--Ricci shrinker with quasi-positive Ricci curvature is compact.
item.dc:creator: Tongxin Xu, Zhenlei Zhang

item.title: Area gaps for minimal surfaces in spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.28317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that a linearly full minimal $2$-torus in $\mathbb{S}^N$ with $N\geq 5$ must have area $>2\pi^2$, and that a linearly full closed minimal surface in $\mathbb{S}^N$ with $N\geq 9$ must have area $>8\pi$. These results verify the Willmore conjecture and the generalized Willmore conjecture in higher codimension for minimal surfaces. The area gaps are obtained by applying the Cheng--Li--Yau comparison theorem and deriving a lower bound of the heat trace, where the monotonicity of the shifted normalized Riesz mean is used. We also establish a volume gap above the balanced Clifford product for linearly full closed minimal $n$-submanifolds in $\mathbb{S}^N$ when $n=3$, $N\geq 9$, or $n\geq 4$, $N\geq 3n-1$.
item.dc:creator: Peng Wang, Zhenxiao Xie

item.title: A note on the cube inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.28390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we adapt ideas from No. 336 of OpenAI's October 6, 2026 mathematics release to prove the weighted cube inequality in all dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Yuchen Bi

item.title: Hyperbolic comparison and rigidity for the hyperspherical radius
item.description: arXiv:2610.28450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Gromov's hyperbolic hyperspherical radius comparison and rigidity conjectures in all dimensions $n\ge3$, without the spin assumption. Let $(X^n, g)$ be a smooth, oriented, connected, compact Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth connected boundary $S$. If ${\rm Sc}_g\ge -n(n-1)$ and $H_S\ge (n-1)\coth R$ for some $R>0$, then ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)\le\sinh R$, with equality if and only if $(X^n,g)$ is isometric to the closed hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$. Under the same curvature bounds, every smooth $1$-Lipschitz map of nonzero degree from $S$ to the boundary of the hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$ extends to an isometry of the fillings. Here, $g_S$ is the induced boundary metric, $H_S$ is the mean curvature of $S$ with respect to the outward unit normal, and ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)$ denotes the hyperspherical radius.
item.dc:creator: Xumin Jiang, Zhehui Wang

item.title: On the Geometry of Low Rank Correlation Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.28475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Correlation matrices of bounded rank form a stratified space whose factor representations lie in a product of spheres. Using the orbit-type description of the rank stratification, we prove that padding factors preserves the Riemannian geometry of each fixed-rank stratum and the intrinsic length metric of every rank-bounded subset. In the reduced model, a Sylvester equation describes the mechanical connection and its horizontal lifts. We derive sectional-curvature formulas and bounds, characterize zero-curvature directions, and determine the connection's holonomy groups. In particular, a flat rank-two connection can have nontrivial dihedral holonomy. For geodesics subject to a rank bound, rank cannot decrease in the interior of a minimizing segment with maximal-rank endpoints; the local excess over the unconstrained quotient distance is controlled by a dimension-independent cubic estimate. Finally, we compute the exact change of measure between quotient Riemannian volume and Euclidean surface volume in the off-diagonal entries. Coarea yields explicit factor densities for both normalized uniform laws.
item.dc:creator: Olivier Bisson, David Loiseaux, Xavier Pennec

item.title: The $\lambda>0$ case for $\Delta u=\lambda-c e^u$ type equation on high dimensional spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.28520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by prescribed Chern scalar curvature problems in complex geometry, we study the equation $\Delta_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}V+\lambda(e^V-1)=0$ with $\lambda>0$ on spheres. For $N\ge4$ and $\lambda>2(N-2)$ with $\lambda\ne2N$, we prove the existence of a nonconstant smooth solution that is axially symmetric and symmetric about the equator.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Li, Qiang Niu, Wubin Zhou

item.title: When is a polynomial in three variables cylindrical?
item.description: arXiv:2609.06465v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a nonconstant polynomial $f\in\mathbb{C}[x_1,x_2,x_3]$ is cylindrical (that is, $f\in\mathbb{C}[x_1,x_2]$ after an invertible linear change of coordinates) if and only if its bordered Hessian determinant vanishes identically. The same conclusion holds over $\mathbb{R}$. We also give explicit counterexamples to this criterion in every dimension $n\ge4$.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojin Lin

item.title: Soft elasticity of soft shells
item.description: arXiv:2610.27263v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.
item.dc:creator: Andre M. Sonnet, Epifanio G. Virga

item.title: Multiplicity of closed geodesics on odd-dimensional bumpy Finsler compact space form
item.description: arXiv:2610.27685v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M = S^{2n+1}/\Gamma$ be a manifold diffeomorphic to a compact space form, endowed with a bumpy Finsler metric $F$. In this paper, we prove that there exist at least $n+3$ contractible minimal closed geodesics on $M$, assuming that all contractible minimal closed geodesics have non-zero Morse indices. Here, a contractible closed geodesic is called minimal if it is not an iteration of any other contractible closed geodesic. In particular, this confirms the generalized Anosov-Katok conjecture for the bumpy quotient manifold $(S^3/\Gamma, F)$ under the non-zero Morse index assumption.
item.dc:creator: Hui Liu, Linxinzi Qi

item.title: Almgren minimality of products of simplex-skeleton cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.27845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we prove that for every $m,n\geq 2$, the orthogonal product $S_m\times S_n\subset\R^m\times\R^n$ is an Almgren minimal cone of dimension $m+n-2$, where $S_k\subset\R^k$ is the cone over the $(k-2)$-skeleton of a regular $k$-simplex. Lawlor and Morgan \cite{LM94} proved the minimality of each $S_k$ by paired calibrations, while Guy David \cite{DJT, GD13} later raised the general question whether products of Almgren minimal sets remain minimal. Our theorem gives a affirmative answer to this product question within the entire Lawlor-Morgan regular-simplex family. It extends the isolated example \(\Y\times \Y\), the product of two 1-dimensional $\Y$ sets, proved in 2014 by the second author, simultaneously to all pairwise products \(S_m\times S_n\), and therefore produces a large new family of possible codimension-two singularities for Plateau's problem. The key idea of the proof is to find a new way to combine homology with paired calibrations in higher codimension. Instead of using only the currents associated with the facets, we consider all their nonzero $\FF$ combinations. The resulting complete family has enough algebraic symmetry to control uniformly the overlaps created by noninjective deformations.
item.dc:creator: Songsong Huang, Xiangyu Liang, Zaoyi Zhang

item.title: The ABC-equation revisited: missed (quasi) integrable cases. Part II: extensions and actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.28009v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We continue here the study of the \textsc{ABC}-equation $Au_xu_{yt} + Bu_yu_{xt} + Cu_tu_{xy} = 0$, $A$, $B$, $C\in\mathbb{R}$ and using the results obtained in the first part construct new quasi-integrable structures and compute their actions on symmetries and cosymmetries.
item.dc:creator: I. S. Krasil'shchik

item.title: Generalized quadratic matrix manifolds: Riemannian geometry and computations
item.description: arXiv:2610.28159v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the set $\mathrm{Gq}(P,Q)$ of real $n\times p$ matrices $X$ satisfying $X^\top Q X = P$, where the nonsingular matrices $P$ and $Q$ are both symmetric or both skew-symmetric and the set is nonempty. Special choices of $P$ and $Q$ yield the Stiefel, generalized Stiefel, indefinite Stiefel, and symplectic Stiefel manifolds, as well as the quadratic matrix Lie groups. We prove that $\mathrm{Gq}(P,Q)$ is a closed embedded submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^{n \times p}$ and that it is compact exactly when $P$ and $Q$ are both symmetric and definite of the same sign. We derive closed-form expressions for its tangent space and, under a canonical-like Riemannian metric, for the normal space, the orthogonal projection, and the Riemannian gradient and Hessian. We extend the Cayley, quasi-geodesic, and polar retractions to $\mathrm{Gq}(P,Q)$, with explicit domains, vector transports, and closed-form second-order corrections. These objects are the ingredients of Riemannian first- and second-order methods. In trace minimization tests with symmetric positive-definite, skew-symmetric, and symmetric indefinite pairs $(P,Q)$, the Riemannian conjugate gradient and trust-region methods reach the same objective value with different retractions and keep the iterates on $\mathrm{Gq}(P,Q)$ up to rounding error.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Peng, Bin Gao

item.title: The Gagliardo-Nirenberg equation on Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.28218v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish geometric and analytic rigidity results for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg equation. On a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature, the existence of a positive critical point of the Gagliardo-Nirenberg quotient forces the manifold to be Euclidean and the solution to be extremal. No minimizing assumption or volume growth hypothesis is required, thereby strengthening earlier rigidity results. In Euclidean space, we prove that all positive solutions of the normalized equation whose nonlinear mass on expanding annuli has sublinear growth are extremals. The linear threshold is optimal, as shown by explicit profiles that are constant in one direction. We also prove a sharp pointwise estimate involving the solution and its gradient, valid without assumptions at infinity, with equality at one point characterizing the extremals. The proofs use weighted divergence identities and a reflection argument controlled by annular mass. Explicit constructions reveal the geometric and variational limits of rigidity: nonflat quotient critical points exist beyond the curvature hypothesis, while the normalized equation admits positive solutions even under strictly positive sectional curvature and maximal volume growth.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Catino, Dario Daniele Monticelli, Alberto Roncoroni

item.title: Learning Normal Coordinates on Riemannian Manifolds with Flow Charts
item.description: arXiv:2610.28302v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Riemannian manifolds are powerful models for problems with non-Euclidean structure. Recent work in geometric machine learning has focused on training deep neural networks to learn Riemannian metrics from high-dimensional data. However, many geometric algorithms require repeated evaluations of the exponential and logarithmic maps, whose high computational cost restricts the utility of learned Riemannian manifolds in practice. We propose to address this cost by training a conditional invertible neural network, called a flow chart, to approximate normal coordinates around points on a given Riemannian manifold. With this approach, the exponential and logarithmic maps can be approximated by fast Euclidean operations in the model's learned coordinate space. Our main contribution is an efficient loss function for training flow charts that is nonnegative and, under suitable domain assumptions, is zero precisely when the chart is normal. Across sixteen synthetic and data-derived geometries, flow charts are competitive with a specialized neural geodesic interpolator for logarithmic map estimation, while also being able to estimate the exponential map. When pretrained, flow charts provide a median speedup of 60-70x over numerical baselines at comparable logarithmic map estimation error, and their learned coordinates improve the accuracy of a numerical geodesic solver.
item.dc:creator: Edmond Cunningham

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.28391v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Singular solutions to the complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation II
item.description: arXiv:2610.28606v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continuing our work in [Math. Ann. 392 (2025), 1503-1518], we construct new singular solutions to the complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation with constant right-hand side in the Bedford-Taylor sense. Let $\mathbb D$ denote the open unit disk in $\mathbb C$. For $n\geq 2$, these solutions include: (i) a bounded solution on $\mathbb D^n$ that is discontinuous almost everywhere and nowhere classically differentiable; (ii) a continuous exhaustion of $\mathbb C^n$ that does not belong to $W^{2,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb C^n)$; (iii) a continuous solution on $\overline{\mathbb D^n}$ whose Laplacian has a singular part. We construct these solutions from singular harmonic functions using partial Legendre transforms and holomorphic pullbacks.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxiang Wang, Wenlong Wang

item.title: Adjusted Connections I: Differential Cocycles for Principal Groupoid Bundles with Connection
item.description: arXiv:2406.16755v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a new perspective on principal bundles with connection as morphisms from the tangent bundle of the underlying manifold to a classifying dg-Lie groupoid. This groupoid can be identified with a lift of the inner homomorphisms groupoid arising in \v{S}evera's differentiation procedure of Lie quasi-groupoids. Our new perspective readily extends to principal groupoid bundles, but requires an adjustment, an additional datum familiar from higher gauge theory. We show that for Lie groupoids, the additional adjustment data amounts to a Cartan connection. The resulting adjusted connections naturally provide a global formulation of the kinematical data of curved Yang-Mills-Higgs theories as described by Kotov-Strobl (arXiv:1510.07654) and Fischer (arXiv:2104.02175).
item.dc:creator: Simon-Raphael Fischer, Mehran Jalali Farahani, Hyungrok Kim, Christian Saemann

item.title: Cut loci of Berger type Lorentzian structures
item.description: arXiv:2505.03514v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consider the deformation of the standard Lorentzian metric on the anti de-Sitter space along the fibers of the Hopf fibration. We study the universal covering of this Lorentzian manifold to exclude a priori presence of time-like cycles. We describe the sets attainable by admissible curves and study the question of the existence of the longest arcs. Next, we investigate Lorentzian geodesics for optimality: we find the cut time and the cut locus. As a geometric application we compute the injectivity radius of the corresponding Lorentzian manifold.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: A.V.Podobryaev. Cut loci of Berger type Lorentzian structures // Analysis and Mathematical Physics. 16, 136 (2026)
item.dc:creator: A. V. Podobryaev

item.title: Superconnections and Bott-Chern valued Riemann-Roch-Grothendieck for complex orbifolds, I
item.description: arXiv:2505.13912v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We use flat antiholomorphic superconnections to study orbifold Chern character following the method introduced by Bismut, Shen, and Wei on general complex orbifolds. We show the uniqueness of orbifold Chern character by proving a Riemann-Roch-Grothendieck theorem for orbifold embeddings.
item.dc:creator: Qiaochu Ma, Xiang Tang, Hsian-Hua Tseng, Zhaoting Wei

item.title: Convexity of mean convex asymptotically conical self-expanders to the mean curvature flow
item.description: arXiv:2509.01023v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove that any $n$-dimensional complete mean convex self-expander of mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq3$, asymptotic to weakly convex cones is strictly convex. As a consequence, each connected component of such a self-expander is properly embedded as an entire graph over a hyperplane, with bounded gradient. We also establish an elliptic positivity criterion for mean convex self-similar solutions, with an application to curvature pinching for asymptotically conical self-expanders.
item.dc:creator: Junming Xie

item.title: Spectral and Schr\"odinger estimates restricted to submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2511.02012v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with nonpositive sectional curvature and smooth bounded geometry. We prove logarithmic spectral projection estimates restricted to uniformly embedded submanifolds. On surfaces with pinched negative curvature, we also prove frequency-independent $L^2\to L^3$ Schr\"odinger restriction estimates on compact geodesic segments for times $c\lambda^{-1}\log\lambda$. If such a surface is even asymptotically hyperbolic, the $L^2\to L^q$ spectral estimates on complete nontrapped geodesics, for $q>2$, gain the square root of the window width. The high-frequency Schr\"odinger estimate holds for all times on these surfaces, both on compact segments and on complete nontrapped geodesics. Under a regularity assumption at the spectral threshold, the all-time estimate holds on the absolutely continuous spectral subspace.
item.dc:creator: Zhexing Zhang

item.title: Properties of Holomorphic $p$-Contact Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2511.10818v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We continue the study of compact holomorphic $p$-contact manifolds $X$ that we introduced recently by expanding the discussion to include non-K\"ahler hyperbolicity issues and a differential calculus based on what we call the Lie derivative with respect to a $(0,\,q)$-form with values in the holomorphic tangent bundle of $X$. We also propose the notion of $p$-contact deformations for which we prove a Bogomolov-Tian-Todorov-type unobstructedness theorem to order two. This kind of small deformations of the complex structure is related to the essential horizontal deformations that we introduced in our previous work and forms part of a wider on-going project aimed at developing a non-K\"ahler mirror symmetry theory that was first tested on the Iwasawa manifold and subsequently on Calabi-Yau page-$1$-$\partial\bar\partial$-manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Hisashi Kasuya, Dan Popovici, Luis Ugarte

item.title: Regularization of singular time-dependent Lagrangian systems
item.description: arXiv:2603.24308v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: One approach to studying the dynamics of a singular Lagrangian system is to attempt to regularize it, that is, to find an equivalent and regular system. In the case of time-independent singular Lagrangians, an approach due to \textit{A. Ibort} and \textit{J. Mar\'in-Solano} is to use the coisotropic embedding theorem proved by \textit{M.J. Gotay} which states that any pre-symplectic manifold can be coisotropically embedded in a symplectic manifold. In this paper, we revisit these results and provide an alternative approach, also based on the coisotropic embedding theorem, that employs the Tulczyjew isomorphism and almost product structures, and allows for a slight generalization of the construction. In this revision, we also prove uniqueness of the Lagrangian regularization to first order. Furthermore, we extend our methodology to the case of time-dependent singular Lagrangians.
item.dc:creator: Manuel De Le\'on, Rub\'en Izquierdo-L\'opez, Luca Schiavone, Pablo Soto

item.title: A mass-type invariant for smooth metric measure spaces and its relation with the fractional Yamabe problem
item.description: arXiv:2606.23248v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On asymptotically Schwarzschild smooth metric measure spaces modeled on the Euclidean half-space, we define a new mass-type invariant analogous to the ADM mass of an asymptotically flat manifold. We prove that this invariant is independent of the choice of admissible asymptotic coordinates. We further show that it fits into a very general framework for mass-type invariants and we also isolate static equations for smooth metric measure spaces under natural boundary conditions. For smooth metric measure spaces obtained through a generalized stereographic projection using the Green's function associated with the fractional Yamabe problem, we identify the mass with the constant term in the asymptotic expansion of the Green's function. This identification gives a geometric interpretation of the constant appearing in the fractional Yamabe problem and recasts its conjectured positivity as a positive-mass-type question.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Almaraz, Levi Lopes de Lima, Shaodong Wang

item.title: A category of locally convex Lie algebroids
item.description: arXiv:2607.07672v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study first-order locally convex Lie algebroids in the setting of Bastiani calculus. The first-order condition is automatic in finite rank, but is an additional regularity hypothesis for general locally convex vector bundles. We define sheaves of scalar-valued and vector-valued Lie algebroid forms as fiberwise continuous alternating maps with smooth local representatives. Morphisms are defined by requiring the induced pullback on inverse-image sheaves of scalar-valued forms to commute with the Lie algebroid differentials. We prove that these algebroids form a category, study representations and cohomology sheaves, and show that the Lie algebroids and morphisms of locally convex Lie groupoids belong to this category. We also give two applications. For a compact manifold $K$, the current algebroid $C^\infty(K,A)\to C^\infty(K,M)$ of a first-order Banach Lie algebroid $A\to M$ is a first-order Fr\'echet Lie algebroid, provided $M$ admits local addition. Finally, we prove a Banach Lie II theorem: a morphism from the Lie algebroid of a locally convex Lie groupoid to that of a Banach-Lie groupoid, both with Hausdorff source fibers, integrates uniquely to a groupoid morphism when the source groupoid is source-connected and source-simply connected.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Gamal Shaltut

item.title: Jacobi polynomials on the simplex of Hermitian matrices and zonal spherical functions on partial flag manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.25760v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the radial part of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on partial flag manifolds and study its eigenfunctions, the elementary zonal spherical functions. These eigenfunctions can be related to orthogonal polynomials on the simplex of Hermitian matrices invariant under simultaneous conjugation by unitary matrices with respect to the complex matrix-variate Dirichlet distribution. Using a matrix-variate version of Koornwinder's method for constructing orthogonal polynomials in multiple variables from orthogonal polynomials in one variable, we construct a family of pairwise orthogonal polynomials in terms of Hermitian Jacobi polynomials and conjecture that some of these are elementary zonal spherical functions. Furthermore, we recall the definition of multivariate Schur polynomials and show how they can be used to obtain information about elementary zonal spherical functions. In particular, we give some partial results in the direction that the radial part of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on partial flag manifolds is strongly triangular with respect to the multivariate Schur polynomials. The elementary zonal spherical functions can then be constructed by applying the Gram-Schmidt orthogonalisation process to the multivariate Schur functions.
item.dc:creator: Teije Kuijper

item.title: Finite-Rank Lie Algebroids for Singular Foliations of Prescribed Vanishing Order
item.description: arXiv:2608.07351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a family of finite-rank Lie algebroids realizing, through their anchor maps, the singular foliations of vector fields vanishing to a prescribed order at the origin. The construction is obtained from the sub-adjacent Lie algebroids of a class of left-symmetric algebroids.
item.dc:creator: Austin Davis, Cheng-Yi Hung, Sangjun Ko, Kaichuan Qi

item.title: A problem for isolated singularities of surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.19452v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbf R^n$ be a set of dimension $2$ with an isolated singular point $0$, such that $E-\{0\}$ is an orientable $\mathcal C^2$ submanifold of $\mathbf R^n$ of dimension $2$, and hence a Riemann surface with the conformal structure induced by the ambient metric. We study the extension of its conformal structure across $0$, under hypotheses that are metric rather than analytic. The main result (1989) is that the isolated singularity $0$ is $\mathit{conformally \ point-like}$ (conformal to a punctured disc) whenever it is $\mathit{$M$-regular}$ : the pair $(E-\{0\},\{0\})$ satisfies a Whitney condition, and the length of the spherical slice $S(0,r)\cap E$ (a curve), where $S(0,r)$ is the sphere of radius $r$ centred at $0$, is bounded above by a linear function of $r$, a condition described as ''metric decay''. This is proven using an argument based on the modulus of rings (extremal length), which generalizes the classical planar technique to $2$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Two classes of examples are examined: surfaces of revolution generated by a 1-dimensional curve and subanalytic sets of dimension 2 ---for which $M$-regularity is proven directly from Hironaka's structure theory---leading to the corollary that every isolated singularity of a $2$-dimensional orientable subanalytic set is conformally point-like. In this case the metric decay condition is obtained from a direct estimate of the volume of the slices $S(0,r)\cap E$ (Lemma 7.5), based on Hironaka's Whitney theorem and Stasica's decomposition into $L$-analytic pieces. A further original result is a $C^\infty$ counterexample showing that a strict Whitney condition alone does $\mathit{not}$ imply the linear length bound: the two hypotheses in the definition of $M$-regularity are independent.
item.dc:creator: Flavio Mosca

item.title: Macroscopic scalar curvature bounds on surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.00186v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the generalized Geroch conjecture, and the corresponding hyperbolic conjecture, in dimension two.
item.dc:creator: Otis Chodosh, Noa Vikman

item.title: The Singular Fibration of Collapsing RCD Spaces with Reifenberg Local Covers
item.description: arXiv:2610.17229v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let compact $\mathrm{RCD}(\kappa,N)$ spaces converge in the measured Gromov--Hausdorff sense, and suppose that they have $(\delta,\rho)$-Reifenberg local covers for one fixed $\rho>0$, with $|\kappa|\rho^2\le1$ and $\delta$ small. We prove that, along a subsequence, the spaces are singular fibrations over the limit: their canonical frame spaces converge to a topological manifold with a locally linear action of $O(n)$ whose quotient is the limit; for large indices the frame spaces fibre over this manifold, by maps that commute with $O(n)$, with fibres homeomorphic to nilmanifolds; and the induced maps to the limit are, near every point, quotients of products by the isotropy group, with fibres homeomorphic to infranilmanifolds. As applications, we extend a fibration theorem of Honda and Zhang to non-smooth RCD spaces whose local covers have injectivity radius bounded below, and we show that for aspherical spaces the isotropy groups are finite, the fibre groups inject into the fundamental groups, and the limit is the quotient of a contractible manifold by a proper cocompact action; under Rong's condition $A_s$ it is a closed aspherical manifold. Three appendices treat smooth manifolds with $\mathrm{Ric}\ge-(n-1)$ and small local rewinding Reifenberg error: a uniform short-time Ricci flow with $|\mathrm{Rm}|\le\alpha/t$, also for complete non-compact data, where it is unique among complete flows with curvature at most $A/t$; a second construction with affine nilmanifold bundles; and, conditional on Nifa's construction, examples showing that rewinding volume control alone does not give continuous Gromov--Hausdorff approximations with small error.
item.dc:creator: Shaosai Huang

item.title: Type I estimates for the K\"ahler-Ricci flow II
item.description: arXiv:2610.22941v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish geometric consequences of our Type I scalar curvature estimate for finite-time solutions of the K\"ahler-Ricci flow on compact K\"ahler manifolds. We prove a uniform global diameter bound and a Type I diameter bound for every fibre of finite time holomorphic contraction. These estimates yield Gromov-Hausdorff convergence to a unique compact metric space homeomorphic to the normal K\"ahler space determined by the limiting cohomology class. We also establish a local partial $C^0$ estimate for the normalized flow and show that the tangent shrinkers are normal complex analytic varieties with log terminal singularities.
item.dc:creator: Wangjian Jian, Jian Song

item.title: Constant mixed Chern curvature on complete type-A flag manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.25864v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the complete flag manifold SU(m)/T m-1, with m >= 3 and its standard complex structure, admits no invariant Hermitian metric with constant mixed Chern curvature when the coefficient of the holomorphic sectional curvature is nonzero. This extends the preceding nonexistence result for a particular Wallach metric on SU(3)/T2 to all invariant Hermitian metrics and to complete type-A flags of arbitrary dimension. Curvature evaluations on holomorphic root spheres contradict a necessary trace identity, covering both Kahler and non-Kahler invariant metrics and excluding both zero and nonzero curvature constants.
item.dc:creator: Yuqin Guo, Dongmei Zhang

item.title: A Lie Bracket on the Space of (Right) Biderivations of a Lie Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2507.12089v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Derivations of a Lie algebra form a Lie algebra under the commutator bracket. Motivated by this property, we investigate Lie algebra structures on spaces of biderivations. We introduce right and left biderivations and show that their spaces admit natural Lie brackets induced by pointwise commutators of derivations. We describe these structures in terms of current Lie algebras and establish a cohomological characterisation of classical biderivations, with applications to semisimple and Heisenberg Lie algebras. We also examine the relation between the right and left brackets for symmetric and skew-symmetric biderivations. Finally, we discuss the pointwise integration of right biderivations into families of Lie group automorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Alfonso Di Bartolo, Gianmarco La Rosa

item.title: Quantization in polarization via transverse Poincar\'e-Birkhoff-Witt theorem
item.description: arXiv:2512.15060v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct, for every prequantizable symplectic manifold $(M,\omega,L)$ equipped with a nonsingular polarization, a deformation quantization $(C_M^\infty[[\hbar]],\star)$ together with a filtered sheaf of subalgebras $C_{M,\hbar}^{(<\infty)}$ that admits an exact action on polarized sections of $L^{\otimes k}$ for each $k\in\mathbb Z^+$. This extends the Kostant--Souriau action of polarization-preserving functions. The main geometric ingredient is a transverse PBW theory associated with a Nirenberg integrable distribution $P$. For any locally free $P$-modules $E$ and $E'$, we construct a PBW isomorphism for the bundle of transverse differential operators from $E$ to $E'$. This extends the PBW theorem for Lie pairs of Laurent-Gengoux--Sti\'enon--Xu to the setting of $P$-modules. After specializing $\hbar= \tfrac{\sqrt{-1}}{k}$, we obtain a sheaf $O_k^{(<\infty)}$ of level-$k$ quantizable functions and prove that its action identifies $O_k^{(<\infty)}$ with the sheaf of transverse differential operators on $L^{\otimes k}$. In the K\"ahler case, this recovers the construction of Chan--Leung--Li. Finally, for standard symplectic tori with real polarizations, we compare our construction with Toeplitz-type operators and obtain their semiclassical asymptotic expansions.
item.dc:creator: Dan Wang, Yutung Yau

item.title: A solution to the Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture through Special Fujita Approximations
item.description: arXiv:2605.30063v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that any big line bundle on a smooth projective variety admits a special Fujita approximation: the volume and the first Riemann-Roch coefficient are both approximated by those of ample $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundles on higher models. Exploiting previous works by Boucksom, Jonsson and Li, we solve the Boucksom-Jonsson Regularization Conjecture on the Non-Archimedean entropy functional. As a main consequence, we obtain a solution to the (uniform version of the) Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture: a polarized smooth projective variety $(X,L)$ admits a cscK metric if and only if it is $\mathrm{Aut}^\circ(X,L)$-uniformly $K$-stable. This extends the known Yau-Tian-Donaldson correspondence for smooth Fano varieties.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Trusiani

item.title: Light rays of Lorentzian graphs and the Born-Infeld model
item.description: arXiv:2609.25449v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Following a program outlined by Bartnik, and also employing nonlinear potential techniques we developed in the last years, we study lightlike singularities of variational solutions to the prescribed Lorentzian mean curvature equation with possibly unbounded (rough) curvature. This corresponds to allowing for unbounded charges in the Born-Infeld model.
item.dc:creator: Cristiana De Filippis, Giuseppe Mingione
